exercise1.prompt: A Car class with wheels shared by every car and a brand of its own

cases.name: wheels belongs to the class, not to one car

hiddenCases.name: Car is a class with an __init__
hiddenCases.describe: a Car class whose __init__ takes the brand

hiddenCases.name: each car keeps its own brand
every car sees the same wheel count
the second car is printed too

exercise1.hint: Ask yourself whether the value would be the same for every car ever made. If it would, it goes in the class body; if it differs per car, it goes on self in __init__. Reading Car.wheels without making a car is the test of which one you wrote.

exercise2.prompt: A Counter that counts how many of itself have been made, read back by a class method

cases.name: three counters were made and counted

hiddenCases.name: get_count is a class method
hiddenCases.describe: a Counter class whose get_count is decorated with @classmethod

hiddenCases.name: the count really goes up with each new counter
the tally is shared, not one per counter

exercise2.hint: self.count += 1 reads the shared value and then writes a new one onto that single counter, leaving the class variable where it was. The line has to change the value on the class itself.

questions.prompt: Where is a class variable written?
choices: In the class body, outside any method
At the top of the file, before the class
questions.explain: It sits in the class body and belongs to the class, so every object made from it sees the same value.

questions.prompt: What is cls in a class method?
choices: The object the method was called on
The module the class lives in
questions.explain: A class method is handed the class rather than an instance, which is why it can be called as Counter.get_count() with no counter at all.

questions.prompt: Match each decorator to what its first parameter receives.
right: the object it was called on
questions.explain: An ordinary method gets self, a class method gets cls, and a static method gets neither -- it just happens to live in the class.

questions.prompt: Counter.count is a class variable. Which lines change the shared tally?
questions.explain: self.count += 1 reads the class value and then writes an instance attribute over it, so the class variable never moves. A bare count is a local name and would raise before it did anything.
